small_guidance:
- The softmax/sigmoid fused kernel is fine but trivial; the dominant cost is the torch ConvTranspose3d. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the tail will not move fast_p meaningfully — at most try num_warps=4 and ensure channels_last memory layout for the softmax read.
- If staying small, add `@triton.autotune` on the softmax kernel over num_warps∈{2,4,8} keyed on C, but expect <5% improvement.
- The real headroom is replacing the conv_transpose; no small tuning will get past fast_p≈0.37.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: for each input element `x[n,ic,d,h,w]`, scatter the outer product `x * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` into the output grid at positions `(d*stride - pad + kd, ...)` accounting for output_padding. Tile over (N, OC, output-spatial) with one program per output tile, gathering contributions from all (ic,kd,kh,kw) — i.e. implement as a gather-style direct conv-transpose (equivalent to a strided im2col GEMM with K = IC*KD*KH*KW).
- Fuse the softmax (along OC=64) and sigmoid into the conv-transpose epilogue: choose tile shape so each program computes a full OC column for one output spatial location (BLOCK_OC=64 fits in registers), enabling in-register max/sum reduction across channels before the sigmoid and store. This eliminates two full passes over the ~16·64·32·64·64 output tensor.
- Fold the conv bias into the GEMM accumulator. Use channels_last (NDHWC) layout for both input and output so OC is the contiguous axis; autotune (BLOCK_M=spatial tile, BLOCK_N=64=OC, BLOCK_K∈{16,32}) with num_warps=4, num_stages=2, verifying SMEM ≤132KB.
